THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
This is an unfortunate case where a person who had lost his land due to compulsory acquisition has been made to suffer for the past nearly 30 years in securing the compensation for his lost land.
2. These facts are not in dispute.
3. On 03.01.1990, Sonubai the wife of Manohar Rao executed an agreement of sale agreeing to sell the suit property in favour of Maheboob Ali (the plaintiff).

After the agreement of sale was executed,
on 19.09.1991, the State issued a notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act proposing to acquire the land for the purpose of Naranja Sugar Factory.
On 01.01.1992, Sonubai executed the registered sale-deed in favour of Maheboob Ali.
Thus, before the lands could be declared to be needed for a public purpose, Maheboob Ali had acquired the title over the suit property under a registered sale-deed.
5. Nearly nine months thereafter i.e., on 01.10.1992 a declaration under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act was issued.

Thereafter, an enquiry regarding the passing of the award was taken-up and the award was submitted to the Deputy Commissioner for approval and the same was approved on 04.01.1992 and the award was declared to have been made on 05.01.1992.

2 6.
It may be pertinent to state here that on 19.10.1992, as per Ex.P.6, Maheboob Ali submitted a representation regarding payment of compensation to the Land Acquisition Officer.

The contents of Ex.P.6 would be relevant and reproduced as follows:-
"May it please your honour, NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322

In response to the Gazette Notification dated 1-10-1992 U/s 6, the claimant/applicant beg to submit as follows :-
1. That the applicant/claimant is the exclusive owner, in possession and enjoyment guntas of village Imampur, tq. Bidar the same having been purchased by me under a valid registered sale-deed from the L.Rs of previous owners.
2. That one Lahoo of Imampur, tq.
Bidar having no concern whatsoever with the said land had the occasion to approach the Hon'ble Court claiming falsely as owner of the said land on the basis of mere fictitious entries got created by him in the R.O.R. by winning over the village officers to his side, without having any right of acquisition therefore behind the back of the real owner.
This claimant has filed a suit before the Hon'ble Munsiff court, Bidar in O.S.No.115/91 restraining the said persons from drawing the compensation amount from the Hon'ble Court.
Whereupon the said court is pleased to grant temporary NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 injunction restraining the said person not to draw the compensation amount in respect of the said land.
The said order is still in force.
Hence, in view of the above facts, it is this claimant only who is entitled to draw the compensation amount in respect of land Sy.No.1/2 of village Imampur, measuring 14 acres 35 guntas.
The applicant/claimant has already submitted all the relevant papers of his exclusive title over the said land on 22.2.92 itself.

But again in the notification dated 4.9.92 the name of said Lahoo has been wrongly shown against the said sy.number without whisper of the applicant's name as claimant atleast to avoid future complication in the matter.

Hence it is prayed that the applicant's name as claimant may kindly be inserted in the said notification and compensation amount in respect of the said land Sy.No.1/2 measuring 14 acres 35 guntas of Imampur village, tq. Bidar may kindly be paid to this claimant, as the opponents have utterly failed to establish their false claim against this claimant, except those fraudulent NC:
2023:KHC-K:5322 entries caused made by them in the RORs without any basis in active collusion and connivance of the village Officers."
7.

It is thus clear that before the award was approved on 04.11.1992 and declared on 05.11.1992,
Maheboob Ali had categorically stated that he had become the exclusive owner of the notified property and had also submitted the relevant papers on 22.02.1992 itself and despite this in the declaration his name had been omitted.

8. The revenue authorities, on the premise that when the notification was issued the name of one Lahu - defendant No.3 was notified, proceeded to disburse the compensation to him, ignoring the fact that there was a sale deed in favour of Maheboob Ali.

sentences.text: The evidence on record indicates that there were revenue proceedings in respect of the entry of Maheboob Ali's name in the revenue records and this was taken advantage of by the Land Acquisition Officer in disbursal of compensation to the third defendant.
The Land Acquisition Officer was examined as DW.1.

During the course of his cross-examination, he has stated as follows :-
"Q.
When plaintiff and defendant No.3 were claiming title over the suit land during the proceedings of land acquisition, how you have decided the title over the property ?
Ans. I did not decide the question of title, right, between the parties, whereas I have accepted all documents, produced by Lahu, showing his ownership right, title and interest.
I have believed 13 years revenue records showing the name of Lahu as the owner and possessor of the land in question and I have accepted upon the report submitted by the V.A., R.I and Tahsildar.
Q:- When the both the parties i.e., the plaintiff and defendant No.3 were fighting over the suit land why you did not refer the matter to the Civil Court ?

NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 Ans. Section 30 of L.A.Act, has enabling provision to refer the matter to the Civil Court, to adjudicate, about the apportionment of the compensation, and not specifically with regard to title.
In this particular case, the plaintiff did not have, any believable evidence, and did not produce before me that evidence I could not refer the matter u/sec.30.

I do not remember, whether the plaintiff has filed his objections, during 6(1)
notification.

It is false to suggest that, even during the time of payment I was with my hand T.I. order, from the Civil Court, restraining the defendant No.3 from taking the compensation amount with regard to suit land/witness says, when the enquiry was held on 22.2.1992, the plaintiff did not produce any T.I order which was continued or extended.

In 1991-92 Revenue Appeal I have directed the Tahasildar, to conduct the re- enquiry, in respect of the claims put-forth by the plaintiff, on the basis of the alleged document said to have been executed by Sonabai.
It is true that, in Ex.P.1 for the land bearing Sy.No.1/2 measuring 22 acres 35 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 guntas in 9 column Manohar S/o Manikrao and in the cultivators column Mallayya Harijan appears.
But in this Ex.P.1, shown to me does not pertain to Lahu, as the extent of Lahu belong to only 14 acres 35 guntas, i.e., suit land."

It may be pertinent to state here that when Maheboob Ali had in fact instituted a suit seeking for an injunction restraining his vendor Sonubai and her son Lahu to restrain them interfering with his possession and in the said suit, he was also granted an interim order restraining the third defendant-Lahu from 13.06.1991 directing Sonubai and Lahu not to enter into any transaction in respect of Sy.No.1/2 and also not to draw the compensation till the next date (as per Ex.P.14).
The said interim order was also extended by the Trial Court as per the order dated 07.03.1992 as per Ex.P.15.

It was therefore clear that there was an order of injunction restraining Lahu from withdrawing the compensation and - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 in gross disobedience to this order, the Land Acquisition Officer proceeded to disburse the compensation.

12. Maheboob Ali ultimately who was forced to approach this Court in view of the disbursal of compensation and the orders of the revenue authorities to seek for a declaration that he was entitled to get the compensation for the acquired lands.

13. The Trial Court on consideration of the evidence came to the conclusion that Maheboob Ali had not been able to establish that he was the owner of the land since he had acquired the land after the publication of the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act.
The Trial Court also held that the State could not have paid the compensation to him and the sale in favour of Maheboob Ali was against public policy.
The Trial Court accordingly dismissed the suit.
14. As against the dismissal of the suit an appeal in *RFA No.709/2001 was preferred by the Maheboob Ali.
This * Corrected vide chamber order dated 28/07/2023.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 Court by order dated 28.06.2007 set-aside the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court and remitted the matter to the Trial Court for fresh consideration.
The Trial Court was directed to dispose of the same in accordance with law.

15. On remand, the Trial Court came to the conclusion that the Maheboob Ali had become the owner of the property by virtue of the sale-deed notwithstanding the fact that the sale-deed had been executed after the publication of the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act.
The Trial Court held that the sale- deed obtained by Maheboob Ali conferred a right to on him to seek for compensation in respect of the land that he had purchased.
The Trial court, accordingly declared that he was the owner in possession of the suit land and that he was entitled for compensation with respect to the said land acquired by the State.

The State was directed to pay the compensation to Maheboob Ali as per his entitlement and also held that the State was entitled to recover the - 12 - Maheboob Ali S/O Wahed Ali @ Chutu Miyan vs The State Of Karnataka Anr on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74944049/
5 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 same from the third defendant who had unauthorizedly received the amount.

sentences.text: 16. Notwithstanding the fact that the competent Civil Court had declared that the Maheboob Ali had acquired title and was entitled to receive compensation, the State instead of taking advantage of the liberty reserved to it to recover the compensation paid to Lahu, proceeded to prefer an appeal questioning the order of the Trial Court.

17. The Appellate Court on re-appreciation of the evidence took the erroneous view that the Trial Court was justified in coming to the conclusion that the Maheboob Ali was the owner of the property, but it proceeded to take the view that the validity of the disbursal of compensation to the third defendant could not be gone into by the Civil Court.

18. It also took the view that the Tahasildar had passed an order on 06.04.1993 calling upon the parties to approach the Civil Court and the suit ought to have been - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 filed within three years, but it had been filed in the year 1997 and therefore the suit was time barred.
19. The Appellate Court accordingly allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit.

As against these judgments, this present second appeal has been filed to consider the following substantial questions of law :
"1. Whether the lower appellate Court has deviated from the issues that had arise before the trial Court whereunder the plaintiff was claiming a right relating to the immovable property based on which the plaintiff was consequently seeking right for the compensation that had been awarded in respect of the property ?

2. Whether in that light, the lower appellate Court was justified in only taking into consideration the date of the award passed for awarding compensation on 05.11.1992 to arrive at a conclusion that in that light the suit was barred by time ?

3. Whether in the facts and circumstances, when the trial Court had taken - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 into consideration with regard to the ownership right that had been claimed to the property, the lower appellate Court was justified in reversing the finding of the trial Court to come to a conclusion that the suit as brought was not maintainable ?"

Maheboob Ali S/O Wahed Ali @ Chutu Miyan vs The State Of Karnataka Anr on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74944049/
6 20.
As stated above, the fact that the lands were acquired and an award was passed is not in dispute.

The only question which was to be adjudicated was as to whether Maheboob Ali was entitled for compensation by virtue of being the owner of the land or the 3rd defendant- Lahu was entitled to withdraw the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer by virtue of being the notified khatedar.
21.
It is also not in dispute that Maheboob Ali acquired title over the suit property under a Sale Deed dated 01.01.1992 executed in his favour by Sonu Bai, the wife of Manikrao and the father of Lahu.
So long as this Sale Deed was not challenged by Lahu, he could not seek for - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 compensation in respect of the land which his mother had conveyed.
22. It is to be stated here that a person who acquires the land after it is notified is disentitled only to challenge acquisition.
He would not however be disentitled to seek for the compensation.

The logic behind this principle is that if a person ventures to purchase the property after it is acquired, he cannot be permitted to agitate the validity of acquisition since he has taken a risk of purchasing a notified property.

23. However, the person who has acquired title, notwithstanding the fact that his acquisition of title was after the 4(1) notification, would merely step into the shoes of true owner of the land and would therefore be entitled to seek for compensation that his vendor was entitled to receive.

24. It is also to be noticed here that the person who sold the land during the pendency of acquisition proceedings - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 would have been compensated by the receipt of sale consideration from the purchaser and therefore, that person i.e., the purchaser would be entitled to seek for compensation.
As a corollary, it is only logical that a person who has acquired title after paying the sale consideration would step into the shoes of the owner and would be entitled to receive the compensation.

It is, therefore, clear that merely because Maheboob Ali purchased the property after the issuance of notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act (for short, referred to as "the Act"), would be debarred from claiming compensation.

25. It may also be pertinent to state here that Maheboob Ali, in the instant case, purchased the property before issuance of the declaration and as on the date of the Sale Deed, the title still remained with his vendor.
In fact, under the provisions of the Act, the land stands vested in the State only on the passing of an award and taking of possession.

In this case, Maheboob Ali purchased the - 17 - Maheboob Ali S/O Wahed Ali @ Chutu Miyan vs The State Of Karnataka Anr on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74944049/
7 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 property on 01.01.1992 and an award was passed only on 05.11.1992.

sentences.text:
Thus,
land would obviously vest in the State thereafter only.
Since the acquisition of land was prior to vesting by Maheboob Ali, he would have to be considered as the true owner of the land and as a consequence, would be entitled to receive the compensation.

26. As regards the view taken by the Appellate Court that the payment of compensation could not be questioned in a civil suit is concerned, it is to be stated here that in the event of dispute regarding the entitlement of compensation, it would be incumbent on the Land Acquisition Officer to refer the matter to the Civil Court under Section 30 of the Act1.
27.

Unfortunately in this case, the Land Acquisition Officer, who was examined, has stated that the matter could not have been referred under Section 30 of the Act because the question of title between the parties cannot Dispute as to apportionment- when the amount of compensation has been settled under Section 11, if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the same or any part thereof, or as to the persons to whom the same or any part thereof, is payable, the Collector may refer such dispute to the decision of the Court.
- 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 be gone into and only the apportionment of compensation can be gone into.
It is on this misconceived notion, in all probability, the Land Acquisition Officer refused to refer the matter to the Civil Court.

Had the Land Acquisition Officer referred the matter to the Civil Court under Section 30 of the Act, Maheboob Ali would not have suffered the travails of the litigation for nearly 30 years and his entitlement to receive the compensation would have been decided under Section 30 of the Act.

In my view, this denial of reference under Section 30 of the Act, though the Land Acquisition Officer was aware of dispute regarding entitlement of compensation, has led to the filing of this civil suit and for this illegality committed by the Land Acquisition Officer, the Civil Court cannot shrug the responsibility and the state that matter of disbursal of compensation cannot be gone into in a civil suit.

28. It is to be stated here that the litigation was started fundamentally because the revenue authorities called upon Maheboob Ali to approach the Civil Court to obtain a - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 declaration of his title and the declaration of his title would be the basis for him to claim compensation.
In other words, Maheboob Ali cannot be penalised for following the dicta of the Tahsildar who directed him to approach the Civil Court to obtain a declaration of his title.

It is, therefore, clear that the finding of the Appellate Court in this regard is incorrect and have to be reversed and it will have to be held that in the present circumstances of this case, in view of the refusal of the authorities to refer the matter under Section 30 of the Act, it was open to the plaintiff to approach the Civil Court and seek for declaration of his title and the consequential declaration that he was entitled to compensation awarded for his land.
The first and third questions of law are accordingly answered in favour of Maheboob Ali, the plaintiff.
Maheboob Ali S/O Wahed Ali @ Chutu Miyan vs The State Of Karnataka Anr on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74944049/

As far as the second question of law as to whether the Appellate Court was justified in taking into consideration the date of the award for arriving at the conclusion that the suit was barred by time is concerned,
- 20 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 it is to be stated here that the plaintiff was seeking for a declaration that he was the owner and for getting such a declaration, the period of three years would not be applicable,
but a period of twelve years under Article 64 of the Limitation Act would be applicable.
In other words, whenever the title of a person is denied and that person seeks for possession, the period of 12 years would be the prescribed period of limitation.
It is no doubt true that in this case, the plaintiff was not seeking for possession, but for compensation.
In my view, since the possession of the property stood translated into compensation awarded for the land, the period of limitation would be 12 years and not 3 years.

30. It is also to be stated here that there were revenue proceedings relating to the land in question and it is only on the conclusion of the proceedings, did Maheboob Ali become entitled to file a suit.
31. As already noticed above, Maheboob Ali was not even required to file a suit since the matter ought to have been - 21 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 referred under Section 30 of the Act.

However, having forced him to litigate,
the State cannot take the plea that the suit was barred by limitation.

The second question of law is,
therefore, answered in favour of Maheboob Ali and against the State.
32. As a consequence of the above, the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court is set aside and the judgment and decree of the Trial Court is restored.

33. However, it is a fact that though the land was acquired way back in the year 1992, the appellant has not been paid the compensation that has been awarded and he has been made to struggle in the Courts for the past nearly 30 years.

I am, therefore, of the view that it would not only be just, but also necessary to direct the State to not only pay the compensation awarded in respect of land in question, but also pay interest at fifteen per cent (15%) per annum on the awarded amount from the date of the award till the date of payment.

I am also of the view that the State by filing an appeal against an order of the Trial Court which reserved liberty to them to recover the compensation from the 3rd defendant Lahu, only prolonged the agony of Maheboob Ali and for this inhuman conduct of the State, in my view, it would be Maheboob Ali S/O Wahed Ali @ Chutu Miyan vs The State Of Karnataka Anr on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74944049/
9 appropriate to impose not only the costs of these proceedings, but also punitive costs of `5,00,000/-.

sentences.text: The said amount shall be paid within a period of three months.
35. The second appeal is accordingly allowed.
36. Liberty is also reserved to the State to proceed against the Land Acquisition Officer, who was responsible for not referring the matter under Section 30 of the Act to the Civil Court.

37. It is to be kept in mind that the State when it disburses compensation to any person, obtains an indemnity bond from the recipient of the compensation to the effect that he would have to refund the compensation, if subsequently a claim has arisen regarding the - 23 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 entitlement to receive compensation.
In my view, therefore, by virtue of this indemnity bond, the interest of the State would not be affected since it may proceed to recover the compensation that it has wrongly paid to another.

38. Learned counsel for the appellant lastly submitted that liberty may be reserved to Maheboob Ali to invoke the provisions under Section 28A of the Act and seek for enhancement of compensation, if there has been an enhancement.
If it is permissible in law to make such an application, at this point of time, the appellant is permitted to make an application under Section 28A of L.A.Act.

However,
the observation made in this order shall not be construed as an extension or an exemption from the provisions of the Limitation Act for the purposes of Section 28A of the Act.

Sd/-

3. Whether in the facts and circumstances, when the trial Court had taken - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5322 into consideration with regard to the ownership right that had been claimed to the property, the lower appellate Court was justified in reversing the finding of the trial Court to come to a conclusion that the suit as brought was not maintainable ?"
The only question which was to be adjudicated was as to whether Maheboob Ali was entitled for compensation by virtue of being the owner of the land or the 3rd defendant- Lahu was entitled to withdraw the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer by virtue of being the notified khatedar.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Maheboob Ali S/O Wahed Ali @ Chutu Miyan vs The State Of Karnataka Anr on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74944049/
6 20.
It is also not in dispute that Maheboob Ali acquired title over the suit property under a Sale Deed dated 01.01.1992 executed in his favour by Sonu Bai, the wife of Manikrao and the father of Lahu.
The logic behind this principle is that if a person ventures to purchase the property after it is acquired, he cannot be permitted to agitate the validity of acquisition since he has taken a risk of purchasing a notified property.
As a corollary, it is only logical that a person who has acquired title after paying the sale consideration would step into the shoes of the owner and would be entitled to receive the compensation.
It is, therefore, clear that merely because Maheboob Ali purchased the property after the issuance of notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act (for short, referred to as "the Act"), would be debarred from claiming compensation.
In fact, under the provisions of the Act, the land stands vested in the State only on the passing of an award and taking of possession.
Since the acquisition of land was prior to vesting by Maheboob Ali, he would have to be considered as the true owner of the land and as a consequence, would be entitled to receive the compensation.
Had the Land Acquisition Officer referred the matter to the Civil Court under Section 30 of the Act, Maheboob Ali would not have suffered the travails of the litigation for nearly 30 years and his entitlement to receive the compensation would have been decided under Section 30 of the Act.
In my view, this denial of reference under Section 30 of the Act, though the Land Acquisition Officer was aware of dispute regarding entitlement of compensation, has led to the filing of this civil suit and for this illegality committed by the Land Acquisition Officer, the Civil Court cannot shrug the responsibility and the state that matter of disbursal of compensation cannot be gone into in a civil suit.
It is, therefore, clear that the finding of the Appellate Court in this regard is incorrect and have to be reversed and it will have to be held that in the present circumstances of this case, in view of the refusal of the authorities to refer the matter under Section 30 of the Act, it was open to the plaintiff to approach the Civil Court and seek for declaration of his title and the consequential declaration that he was entitled to compensation awarded for his land.
